entries.title: Renal Anatomy, Embryology, and Hemodynamics

testable_competencies.classification: Classify basic renal embryologic origin, gross/microscopic structure, and hemodynamic autoregulation (afferent/efferent arteriolar tone, RAAS) as background for the diagnostic-approach competencies tested in every subsequent unit (AKI, glomerular disease, HTN).

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational anatomy/physiology background, not independently testable at the MCCQE level; frames the AKI/glomerular-disease/hypertension competencies tested in later units.

entries.title: Assessment of Renal Function: GFR Measurement, Urinalysis, Urine Microscopy, and Urine Biochemistry

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 8's key/enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'interpret a urinalysis, paying attention to differentiating glomerular from nonglomerular causes' and to order 'a urinalysis and urine microscopy' - this unit's urinalysis/microscopy interpretation competency is a direct, named component of that objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1's enabling objectives name 'urine specific gravity, urinalysis, serum and urine electrolytes' as critical investigations for AKI; this unit's urine-biochemistry/FENa interpretation competency directly supports that diagnostic pathway.

testable_competencies.interpretation: Interpret urinalysis (dipstick), urine microscopy (casts, crystals, cells), and urine biochemistry (electrolytes, FENa, osmolality) to distinguish glomerular from nonglomerular disease and prerenal from intrinsic renal causes of reduced function.
testable_competencies.calculation: Calculate/interpret eGFR and creatinine clearance as measures of renal function.

entries.title: Sodium Disorders: Hyponatremia, Hypernatremia, and Diabetes Insipidus

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 99-2 is titled and scoped directly for hyponatremia diagnosis/severity/complications/management, matching this unit's testable content exactly.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 99-1 is titled and scoped directly for hypernatremia; the objective's rationale explicitly notes most cases occur due to water depletion, matching this unit's diabetes-insipidus/water-balance content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Diabetes insipidus is a named cause of polyuria under objective 110-2's causal conditions; this unit's DI diagnostic-approach competency (water deprivation test, urine osmolality) is a component of that broader polyuria workup.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of hyponatremia and hypernatremia using volume status assessment and urine/serum osmolality.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan for symptomatic vs. asymptomatic hyponatremia/hypernatremia, including correction-rate safety limits to avoid osmotic demyelination/cerebral edema.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize diabetes insipidus (central vs. nephrogenic) as a cause of hypotonic polyuria and hypernatremia.

entries.title: Potassium Disorders: Hyperkalemia and Hypokalemia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 79-1 is titled and scoped directly for hyperkalemia, explicitly requiring recognition of ECG-abnormality-associated urgency, matching this unit's core testable content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 79-2 is titled and scoped directly for hypokalemia, explicitly requiring recognition of severe-muscle-weakness/ECG-abnormality urgency, matching this unit's core testable content.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of hyperkalemia and hypokalemia.
testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize ECG changes and life-threatening presentations of severe hyperkalemia/hypokalemia requiring urgent treatment.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate emergency treatment for hyperkalemia (calcium stabilization, insulin/glucose, shift/elimination therapies) and appropriate repletion for hypokalemia.

entries.title: Phosphate and Magnesium Disorders: Hyperphosphatemia, Hypophosphatemia, Hypermagnesemia, and Hypomagnesemia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for phosphate or magnesium disorders specifically; targeted registry searches for 'phosphate' and 'magnesium' returned zero matches. Retained as a loose secondary anchor since CKD's enabling objectives explicitly name calcium/phosphate disorder management as part of CKD complication management, and this unit's content (AKI/CKD as the dominant etiology of hyperphosphatemia/hypermagnesemia) is presented in that context in the source text.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize phosphate and magnesium disorders as complications of AKI/CKD and other conditions, and their characteristic clinical/ECG findings.

entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: Evidence retained despite WEAK strength because phosphate/magnesium disorders recur as a CKD-management sub-competency explicitly named in objective 89-2's enabling objectives, distinguishing this from a SPECIALIST_DETAIL/no-evidence classification.

entries.title: Acid-Base Disorders: Metabolic Acidosis and Metabolic Alkalosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 45 is titled and scoped directly for acid-base abnormalities, explicitly naming high anion gap metabolic acidosis as a particular focus, matching this unit's core testable content (anion gap calculation, osmolar gap, compensation rules).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis using anion gap, osmolar gap, and expected compensation.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan, particularly for high anion gap metabolic acidosis and its life-threatening causes (e.g. toxic alcohol ingestion, DKA).

entries.title: Polyuria: Diagnostic Approach

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 110-2 is titled and scoped directly for polyuria diagnosis/severity/complications/management, matching this unit's core testable content (urine osmolality-based diagnostic algorithm).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose the cause of polyuria using a stepwise urine-osmolality-based approach (water diuresis vs. osmotic diuresis vs. mixed).

entries.title: Acute Kidney Injury: Classification, Prerenal/Renal/Postrenal Approach, and Management

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1 is titled and scoped directly for AKI, explicitly requiring diagnosis of cause/severity/complications and recognition of situations requiring urgent intervention (dialysis, fluid resuscitation) - matching this unit's core content (KDIGO AKI staging, prerenal/renal/postrenal differentiation, indications for dialysis) exactly.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Volume overload/edema is a named complication and clinical feature of AKI in this unit; objective 29-1's causal conditions plausibly encompass AKI-related fluid retention.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose AKI using the KDIGO staging criteria (serum creatinine change and urine output) and differentiate prerenal, intrinsic renal, and postrenal etiologies using history, urine microscopy, and FENa.
testable_competencies.management: Construct an initial management plan including correction of prerenal factors, discontinuation of nephrotoxic drugs, treatment of complications (fluid overload, hyperkalemia, acidosis), and recognition of indications for urgent dialysis.

entries.title: Glomerular Disease: Nephritic/Nephrotic Syndrome Classification and Major Glomerulonephritides

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 8's causal conditions explicitly list glomerular disease (SLE, HUS, vasculitis) as a category the candidate must differentiate from nonglomerular hematuria; this unit's nephritic-syndrome/glomerulonephritis content directly supports that differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's nephrotic syndrome content (Table 12: minimal change, membranous, FSGS, MPGN) is the paradigmatic glomerular cause of proteinuria that objective 84 requires the candidate to diagnose and manage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1's causal conditions explicitly list glomerulonephritis and TTP-HUS as renal (intrinsic) causes of AKI; this unit's RPGN content directly supports that etiologic category.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate nephritic from nephrotic syndrome presentations using clinical features (hematuria/RBC casts vs. edema/heavy proteinuria) and recognize rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis as a nephrology emergency.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the major glomerulonephritis/nephrotic-syndrome entities (minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy, FSGS, MPGN, IgA-associated vasculitis) and their characteristic secondary associations.

entries.title: Tubulointerstitial Disease: Acute Interstitial Nephritis and Acute Tubular Necrosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1's causal conditions explicitly list 'Tubulointerstitial (e.g., acute tubular necrosis, interstitial nephritis)' as a named renal (intrinsic) AKI category, matching this unit's content exactly.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize acute interstitial nephritis (drug-induced, urine eosinophils) and acute tubular necrosis (ischemic or nephrotoxic) as the major intrinsic-renal causes of AKI and distinguish them by history and urine microscopy.

entries.title: Vascular Diseases of the Kidney: Renal Artery Stenosis, Thrombotic Microangiopathy, and Calcineurin Inhibitor Nephropathy

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1's causal conditions list 'Vascular (e.g., cholesterol emboli)' as a renal (intrinsic) AKI category; this unit's renal artery stenosis/TMA/calcineurin-nephropathy content is a component of that vascular-cause differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 9-1's causal conditions explicitly list 'vascular (e.g., unilateral renal artery stenosis)' as a secondary hypertension cause; this unit's renal artery stenosis content directly supports that secondary-HTN workup.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize renal artery stenosis, thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP-HUS spectrum), and calcineurin inhibitor nephropathy as vascular causes of renal dysfunction and their distinguishing investigations.

entries.title: Analgesic Nephropathies: NSAID- and Acetaminophen-Induced Renal Syndromes

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: NSAID-induced vasomotor AKI is a named mechanism under objective 89-1's prerenal/functional causal category (renal hypoperfusion); this unit's analgesic-nephropathy content is a component of that etiologic differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize NSAID- and acetaminophen-associated renal syndromes (vasomotor AKI, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis, papillary necrosis) and their reversibility with drug discontinuation.

entries.title: Systemic Diseases with Renal Manifestations: Diabetic Nephropathy, Scleroderma Renal Crisis, Multiple Myeloma, and Malignancy-Associated Renal Disease

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Diabetic nephropathy is the single most common cause of ESRD per this unit's content, and CKD staging/management (objective 89-2) is the renal-specific competency tested when these systemic diseases present with renal involvement.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize diabetic nephropathy, scleroderma renal crisis, myeloma-associated renal disease, and malignancy-associated renal disease as renal manifestations of systemic disease, and identify indications suggesting a non-diabetic cause of renal disease in a patient with diabetes.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Scleroderma renal crisis and multiple myeloma renal involvement are explicitly cross-referenced in the source text to Rheumatology (RH14) and Hematology (H51) respectively for full disease management; this unit is scoped to the renal-manifestation-recognition competency only, not primary-disease management, deferred to the global cross-chapter overlap audit per project convention (see MI's SU-MI-12/16/20/25 precedent in review_items.json).

entries.title: Chronic Kidney Disease: KDIGO Staging, Complications, and Management

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-2 is titled and scoped directly for CKD diagnosis of cause/stage/complications and management planning, matching this unit's core testable content (KDIGO staging, complication management, indications for renal replacement therapy) exactly.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose and stage CKD using GFR category and albuminuria (KDIGO 2024 criteria) and identify the underlying cause.
testable_competencies.management: Construct a comprehensive management plan for CKD progression prevention (BP/glycemic control, RAAS blockade, SGLT2i) and complications (anemia, mineral bone disease, metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia).

entries.title: Hypertension: Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis, Renovascular Hypertension, and Renal Parenchymal Hypertension

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 9-1 is titled and scoped directly for hypertension diagnosis/severity/complications/management, and its causal conditions explicitly name renal parenchymal disease and renal artery stenosis - matching this unit's core content (hypertensive nephrosclerosis, renovascular HTN, renal parenchymal HTN) exactly.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content explicitly frames CKD-hypertension as bidirectional (HTN causes nephrosclerosis; CKD-driven Na+ retention worsens HTN), a component of the comprehensive CKD management competency in objective 89-2.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate chronic (benign) from malignant hypertensive nephrosclerosis using clinical picture, urinalysis, and target-organ-damage findings; recognize renovascular hypertension as a secondary, potentially reversible cause.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate BP-target-appropriate management for hypertensive nephrosclerosis and recognize when malignant hypertension requires urgent BP-lowering.

entries.title: Cystic Kidney Diseases: Adult Polycystic Kidney Disease, Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease, and Medullary Sponge Kidney

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for polycystic/cystic kidney disease specifically. ADPKD is a named, progressive cause of CKD/ESRD in this unit's content (up to 50% reach ESRD by age 60), making objective 89-2's cause-diagnosis component the closest direct anchor.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hematuria (microscopic or gross) is described as a frequent presenting sign of ADPKD in this unit's content, a component of the hematuria-cause differential in objective 8.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the presentation of ADPKD (family history, hematuria, flank pain, HTN, palpable kidneys, extrarenal manifestations) and its diagnostic confirmation by imaging, and distinguish it from ARPKD and medullary sponge kidney by inheritance pattern and age of presentation.

entries.title: End-Stage Renal Disease: Definition, Risk Factors, and Uremic Presentation

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ESRD is the terminal stage (G5) of the CKD spectrum defined by objective 89-2's staging framework; this unit's uremic-presentation-recognition competency is a direct, named component of diagnosing CKD complications.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the multi-system presentation of uremic syndrome (volume overload, electrolyte abnormalities, cognitive/GI/hematologic/endocrine manifestations) as an indication for renal replacement therapy.

entries.title: Renal Replacement Therapy: Dialysis Modalities, Indications, and Complications

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for dialysis specifically (targeted registry search for 'dialysis' returned zero matches). Objective 89-2's management scope explicitly includes 'renal replacement therapy' as a management-plan component; retained as a moderate-strength anchor since this unit's peritoneal-dialysis-vs-hemodialysis comparison and complication-recognition content is the operational detail underlying that management competency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1's enabling objectives explicitly require assessing 'the need for urgent intervention (e.g., dialysis...)' and 'determining whether the patient requires specialized care (indications for dialysis)' - this unit's dialysis-indications content is a direct component of that AKI management competency.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize indications for urgent/chronic dialysis and select an appropriate modality (peritoneal dialysis vs. hemodialysis) based on patient factors.
testable_competencies.complications: Recognize dialysis-associated complications (disequilibrium syndrome, catheter-related infection/bacteremia, hemodynamic instability).

entries.title: Renal Transplantation: Indications, Immunosuppression, and Complications

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for renal transplantation specifically. Objective 89-2's causal-conditions/management scope for CKD explicitly names 'collaboration with specialists as indicated' and renal replacement therapy as a management endpoint for ESRD; retained as a moderate-strength anchor since transplantation is the definitive renal-replacement management option this unit covers.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize renal transplantation as the preferred renal replacement modality for eligible ESRD patients and identify the major post-transplant complications requiring recognition (graft rejection, opportunistic infection, malignancy, new-onset diabetes).

entries.title: Common Nephrology Medications: Diuretics and Related Agents

testable_competencies.classification: Classify the site of action, mechanism, indications, and dosing framework of loop diuretics and related nephrology medications as background pharmacology underlying the fluid-management competencies tested in AKI/CKD/electrolyte-disorder units.

entries.zero_question_reason: Medication-table reference content (specific dosing figures); not independently testable at the MCCQE level as isolated pharmacology facts, and current dosing guidance is not encoded into the scope layer per project instructions (see freshness note in unresolved_mappings.json).
